doc.summary: Batched pipe I/O for the view codec. write_view/read_view move one int32 block and one length-prefixed string at a time: ~46 000 read(2) and as many write(2) calls for a single Wikipedia page, each a context switch for 4-64 bytes.
doc.description: Inside those two functions the traffic goes through a per-THREAD 64 KiB buffer instead (no state is shared: the async tick thread and the caller each have their own). The byte stream is unchanged. Writes are flushed before write_view returns. A read buffer may hold the bytes that follow the view in the same reply: they stay in it and the next read on that fd consumes them first, so no byte is ever lost; the protocol is request/response lockstep, so nothing beyond the reply can be in the pipe.

doc.description: An XHR/fetch from page script is proxied to the TRUSTED parent over the existing pipes: write a TAG_SUBREQ frame, block for the parent's reply. The parent re-applies the FULL network policy (host blocklist/tracker filter, realm routing, TLS-PQ) before fetching, so a compromised worker still cannot reach a blocked host. Refused/over-budget/IO-error => non-zero (XHR completes with status 0). Only callable inside a page-load script window (net_active) so it never desyncs the OP_EVAL/OP_DECODE_IMAGE response paths.
